$comment: The TrueNorth character rig contract, task 1.11. NORMATIVE: assets/style/rig-contract.md is the prose;
this file is the same contract as data, and it is what the contract tests load.
It is authored under assets/ because assets/** is the art agent boundary. content/schemas/rig.schema.json
(ADR-0017) validates this shape and tests/unit/contracts/rig-is-coherent.test.ts reads it from here.
content/characters/rig.json - the path CLAUDE.md names - EXISTS and is a byte-for-byte mirror of this
file except for its $schema, which is relative to content/. The two are edited together, in the same
commit, or the rig has two live copies and no gate can tell you which one is stale.
Every name here appears IDENTICALLY in the Rive file and in the sprite atlas. That identity is the
whole point of ICharacterRenderer: gameplay code must not be able to tell which backend it got.

The `{mode}` brace on four parts, and every state named `<mode>/<state>`, are the LEVEL's locomotion mode made visible. `mode` is NOT a slot: it joins `expression` as a brace naming something the character does not choose, which is what app/adapters/phaser/locomotion-pose.ts binds and what keeps the slot-independence product a statement about player choices. rig-contract.md 11 is the prose and carries what is deliberately not here - a horse, a train seat, a brake.

characterSpace.note: Part windows are given in THIS space, so a window origin IS the part offset. To place a character at world (x, y) with its feet on the ground, draw each part at (x - 120 + frame.x, y - 460 + frame.y). THE VIEW IS PART OF THIS SPACE: every character is drawn three-quarter with the canonical facing RIGHT, the body about 40 degrees off strict profile and the HEAD at the same three-quarter with the whole face on its leading half (art-bible.md 7.7; it was turned to about 25 before 2026-09-14), because this is a side-scroller and a figure that faces the camera cannot read as travelling. Screen x is therefore the FORE-AFT axis, which is what makes the walk cycle swing at full amplitude, and the near side is the wearer RIGHT - so the -r parts draw last. See art-bible.md 7.1 and rig-contract.md 1.

artboards.note: Generic constable. Never named as a member of a real force, and the artboard carries no crest, wordmark, collar dog, shoulder flash, chevron or service number.

The beaver guide: the companion who appears at points of interest and leads the learning moments. It plays the SAME rig, the same state machine and the same four expressions as every person in the game, and it stands to the same 6-head canon - costume distinguishes characters, stature never does (art bible 7). `skin`, `hairShape` and `hairColour` fall back like any NPC document and are inert here: `head-shell-beaver` covers the shared head and the short crop entirely, which is why no pelt tone was added to the skin slot. It is a companion animal, never a stand-in for a person: docs/content-review.md applies to it as it does to everything else.

inputs.name: grounded
inputs.meaning: Feet are on the ground polyline.

inputs.name: moving
inputs.meaning: The traversal system wants forward motion (hold-to-move, or auto-move).

inputs.name: talking
inputs.meaning: A dialogue or question card owns this character.

inputs.name: reducedMotion
inputs.meaning: Suppress squash-and-stretch and hold the idle key. Set by the caller from settings; the renderer never reads settings itself.

inputs.name: speed
inputs.meaning: Horizontal speed normalised to this character top speed. Selects walk below 0.55 and run at or above it.

inputs.name: verticalSpeed
inputs.meaning: Vertical velocity normalised: positive rising, negative falling. Only read while grounded is false.

inputs.name: interact
inputs.meaning: Fired when the player taps an NPC or a POI in range.

selector.note: First match wins. This is the Rive state machine written out, and it is exactly what a sprite adapter evaluates - same inputs, same order, same answer. A contract test can drive both backends through this table and compare the selected state.

rules.when: interact fired and its state has not finished
land fired and its state has not finished and not reducedMotion

expressions.note: setExpression(name) resolves the {expression} template variable. Every pose differs in the SHAPE of brow, pupil and mouth, so it survives greyscale, high contrast and the plain Canvas tier, which has no Filter pipeline (ADR-0011).

events.name: footfall
events.when: Each foot plant in walk and run, at t 0.0 and 0.5.
events.use: Step audio and its subtitle equivalent.

events.name: interactReach
events.use: The moment the POI or dialogue opens, so art and UI agree.

events.name: landImpact
events.when: t 0.0 of the land state. Still fired under reducedMotion even though the state is skipped.
events.use: Impact audio, camera shake where enabled.

skin.note: The six ramps ship UNNAMED here: naming is docs/content-review.md 8.1 and OQ-REVIEW-6, not art. fallback is for NPC documents and save recovery only; it is arbitrary (the middle of the ordinal ramp) and the creator never renders it as a pre-selection - it randomises uniformly on open.

headCovering.note: The toque is the FALLBACK, which is what an unchosen slot resolves to: an NPC document, a save being repaired, and every figure the game spawns before the character creator is wired (app/adapters/phaser/level-scene.ts falls back artboard skins -> slot fallback). The player therefore meets a figure in a toque rather than a bare-headed one. It stays playerSelectable and `none` stays an option: the creator's range is not reduced, and assets/refs/references.json still requires a bare-headed run in every art hand-off, because a costume that only reads with a hat on has not been checked.

costume.note: Not player-selectable, so it is outside the slot-independence product: it says WHICH character this artboard is, not how a player customised one. `beaver` is the guide's pelt, and it drives four parts no human artboard resolves - tail, head-shell, muzzle and the bare hide of the paws and hind feet.

presentation.note: Opened 2026-09-14. The product owner answered OQ-ART-08 and OQ-LEVEL-3 directly - "the character has no gender" - by asking for the choice, so the slot has three options. It is a slot on the ONE artboard with the ONE proportion canon: presentation is carried by face detail inside the head outline (brow shape and weight, lashes, a lip mark, cheek and jaw shading) through the `face-{expression}-{presentation}` template, never by limb length, body width, height or head size. Choosing one sets no other slot; every option stays independently adjustable, and every presentation is available with every skin, hair shape, hair colour, head covering and feature (docs/content-review.md 8.2). `neutral` is a look of its own, not the absence of a choice. The fallback is `neutral` because an NPC document or a repaired save must not acquire a presentation nobody chose. playerSelectable is true and the player artboard lists it last in playerSelectableSlots, which is the order the creator draws. A save written before this slot opened names no presentation: it takes the fallback and is not a repair, because the player lost no choice.

slotIndependence.rule: Every option in every slot is available with every option in every other slot.
slotIndependence.checkable: The product of the option counts equals the number of valid combinations; no part frame template names two slots that constrain each other. hairShape and hairColour are separate slots for exactly this reason: one slot of 20 combined options could hide a coupling.

parts.name: mount-deck
parts.note: The body of whatever the level's locomotion mode put under the character, drawn BEHIND the figure and in front of the contact shadow: a toboggan under a seated rider, a board under two boots, a bicycle under both. It carries its own transform rather than a foot's, because a deck stays flat on the ground while the feet move on it. `{mode}` is the brace app/adapters/phaser/locomotion-pose.ts binds; a mode that authors no frame draws nothing here, which is the same rule every "none" option already uses and needs no branch in either backend.

parts.name: tail
parts.note: The guide’s paddle tail. `tail-parka` and `tail-serge` are absent from `frames`, so the part draws nothing on every human artboard - the same mechanism every "none" option uses, and no special case in either backend. Carried out to the wearer’s right, which in a right-facing three-quarter pose is the TRAILING side, so it streams out behind the animal instead of hiding behind its body.

parts.name: foot-gear-l
parts.note: Equipment strapped to the wearer's left boot - the FAR one. It shares `foot-l`'s pivot and carries `foot-l`'s transform in every key of every state, which is what makes it rigid with the boot on a rig that parents nothing. Drawn AFTER the boot so a skate holder closes over the sole, which is where a holder actually sits.

parts.name: foot-gear-r
parts.note: Equipment strapped to the wearer's right boot - the NEAR one. Same rule as `foot-gear-l`: `foot-r`'s pivot, `foot-r`'s transform, drawn after the boot.

parts.name: neck
parts.note: A part, not a shaped extension of either mass it joins, because it has to be occluded from BOTH ends: the coat collar closes over its base (torso draws after it) and the jaw closes over its top (head draws before it). Neither a torso that grew a stub nor a head that grew one can be covered at the other end, and the head-on-shoulders read is exactly what that costs. Pivot at the neck ROOT, so its rotation is the average of the chest's and the head's - the head still turns further than the body, and the neck is what makes that turn legible instead of a detached head. `neck-parka`, `neck-serge` and `neck-beaver` do not exist: the neck is skin, so it resolves on {skin} like the head, and the guide's pelt covers it exactly as `head-shell-beaver` covers the shared head and the short crop. Its window is 34x35 at (103,104) and every pixel of it outside y 121..134 is covered: 11 px hidden under the jaw, 4.5 px hidden under the collar. That margin is what absorbs the relative motion the keyframes put between chest and head, which is (head.ty - torso.ty)/2 and is at worst 0.8 px upward (`talk` t 0.5) and 1.5 px downward (`land` t 0.55). The lower bound on the window is the collar; the UPPER bound is `head-shell-beaver`, which must CONTAIN this window or make verify-art refuses the guide's not-applicable claim for `skin`.

parts.name: mount-fore
parts.note: The part of the equipment that is NEARER the camera than the rider: a toboggan's curled prow, and the hauling end of anything else that has one. Last in z for that reason. Without it the identifying end of a sled is behind the shins that are folded over it, which is the whole read at phone size.

atlas.rule: A part whose resolved template is not in "frames" draws nothing. That is how every "none" option works, and it needs no special case in either backend.
atlas.note: assets/src/svg/shared/character/<name>.svg becomes atlas frame key character-<name> (scripts/assets.mjs, shared owner). The Rive file uses the SAME strings as its slot names.

idle.note: Breathing only: the torso rises 1.6 px and the head 2. The rest pose is a three-quarter stand, and since 2026-09-14 not a mannequin: the elbows are soft, the arms hang a little clear of the coat and the feet stand 12 px apart. The pair still cannot hold a stride without crossing over itself, so the stride stays in the walk keys. Under reducedMotion the state holds key 0.

walk.note: A side-scroller walk, solved by forward kinematics from the hip and the shoulder. Screen x is the fore-aft axis in this view, so the swing is horizontal and reads at phone size; the near arm opposes the near leg. Contact at t 0 and t 0.5 is where `footfall` fires.

run.note: The same cycle at 1.45x amplitude and 0.69x duration, with the torso leaning further into the run.

jump-rise.note: Arms and knees in opposite poses, not just an offset: the state has to read on the plain tier, which has no filters.

jump-fall.note: The mirror image of jump-rise at the shoulder and the knee, so rise and fall differ in SHAPE and not in height alone.

land.note: The only squash-and-stretch in the rig: both knees fold and the body drops 12 px. Under reducedMotion this state is skipped entirely and the machine goes straight to the next one, which is why the selector tests it before anything else.

talk.note: The near-side hand comes up and the head tilts. Dialogue text is DOM and carries the words; this state only says WHO is speaking, which is why it is shape and not a glow.

interact.note: The near arm reaches forward, along the direction of travel, so the gesture points at what was tapped.

skate/idle.note: A two-foot glide, and it is deliberately NOT a stand. `moving` is the traversal system's INTENT, not the skater's velocity, and Ottawa's ice returns 0.9 of the momentum on release - so this is the state a coasting skater is in for most of a crossing. Knees soft, weight over the near skate, torso 14 degrees into the direction of travel. It reads correctly stopped as well, which is what a ready stance is.

skate/walk.note: Two strokes per cycle, 1100 ms, and this state exists because a walk cycle on a canal is the defect a player reported from the live site. What carries it at 390 px, in the order the cues survive being made small: the trailing skate LIFTED clear of the ice and swung back, the 24-degree body pitch, the deep bend in the supporting knee, and the arms swinging fore and aft at full length. Contact is at t 0 and t 0.5, where `footfall` fires - one push per half cycle. The far leg's push extends further than the near leg's (52 degrees against 44) because the far hip sits 24 px forward in this three-quarter view, so an identical angle would swing the near skate off the left edge of character space.

skate/run.note: The same cycle at 0.72x duration with three more degrees of pitch. It is a separate declaration and not a fallback: the selector picks `run` above `speed` 0.55, and a skater who reverted to the rig's own running cycle at speed would be the reported defect returning at the exact moment the player is going fastest.

toboggan/idle.note: The same seated posture as `toboggan/walk` with the recline taken out - 18 degrees instead of 27 - because a stopped sled at the top of the run still has a rider sitting on it. There is no standing idle for this mode: a tobogganer who stops does not stand up through the sled, and a level that wants the player on their feet sets the mode back to `walk`.

toboggan/walk.note: Seated, reclined 27 degrees, knees folded up, feet tucked back on the deck - the posture in `refs/quebec-city/toboggan-slide-riders.jpg` and the same one the two background riders in `quebec-city/layer-60-slope.svg` hold, so the player matches the level rather than arriving from a different game. The whole figure drops 131 px and moves 28 px back: a seated rider's hips are at the deck, and the sled reaches further forward than the rider does. THE LEGS CANNOT REACH FURTHER FORWARD THAN THIS. 98 + 74 px of leg from a hip 19 px above the deck folds to about 70 px of forward reach, which is why the knees are up rather than out, and it is also why the prow is a separate part: at full extension the shins cross the front of the sled.

toboggan/run.note: IDENTICAL KEYS TO `toboggan/walk`, under a second name, and that is the point rather than an oversight. A sled does not change posture when it goes faster, and without this declaration the selector would stand a seated rider up the moment `speed` passed 0.55.

skateboard/idle.note: The rolling stance with the arms brought in, and not a stand: this seawall's `glide` is 0.62, the highest in the game, and a released input coasts. FRONT foot (far, left) over the front truck, BACK foot (near, right) over the rear truck, 92 px between the ankles - the wheelbase of the deck under them - because that is where a rider's feet go (assets/refs/vancouver/skateboard-rider-in-winter-coat.jpg, CC0). The figure is lifted 30 px onto a deck whose top is 36 px off the ground; the other 6 are the knees, bent about 25 and 33 degrees with the knee FORWARD. No leg crosses the other. The boots point the way the character travels, as every foot in this rig does: a flat rig cannot foreshorten a foot turned across the board, and that is recorded as a simplification rather than drawn wrong.

skateboard/walk.note: Cruising. Same feet on the same trucks; the body drops 3 px into the knees and pitches 9 degrees over the front foot, the LEADING (far) arm reaches forward and the trailing (near) arm hangs back, which is the balance the reference shows. Three keys, 0 and 1 identical, so the motion is a bob along one line and has no loop direction to get wrong.

skateboard/run.note: The same stance lower and further over the board: lifted 21 px instead of 30, 14 degrees of pitch, arms wider. The feet do not move on the deck at speed.

bike/idle.note: Stopped, still astride, feet still on the pedals. A cyclist who stops does not stand beside the bicycle unless the level dismounts them, which is what setting the mode back to `walk` does.

bike/walk.note: One pedal revolution per 900 ms cycle, the four keys at the quarter positions. Hands are solved to the bar and feet to the pedals by two-link inverse kinematics rather than by eye, because a hand 6 px off a handlebar is the one error this pose cannot survive - invisible in the SVG, obvious in the render. The torso folds 22 degrees over the bar; more than that and the arms cannot reach it - 68 + 68 px of arm from a shoulder carried forward by the fold is 136 px, and the bar is 132 px away at this angle. That number is the reason this rider is not drawn in a racing crouch.

bike/run.note: The same revolution at 0.68x duration and three more degrees of fold, which is still inside the arm's reach.

train/idle.note: A passenger seated in the dome of a Park car (ADR-0031). The feet rest flat on the sole line, which is the ride's floor: the level places the car so its `riderAnchor` is under them, and a seated pose with no car under it is a figure sitting in mid-air, which is why no level may declare `train` without a ride. Thighs forward, shins near vertical, the upper body reclined 3 degrees and carried with the shoulders and head, hands on the lap by two-link IK. The hips drop 91.34 px from standing. Breathing only, as `idle`.

train/walk.note: The same keys as `train/idle`, on purpose. A passenger does not change posture when the train moves, and the train supplies the movement: the ties go by under it and the ride rocks on its bob, which reduced motion holds still. Declared rather than left to fall back, because the fallback is the standing walk cycle, and a figure striding inside a dome is the defect this pose exists to fix.

train/run.note: The same keys again: the selector picks `run` above speed 0.55 and the train cruises above it, so without this the passenger would stand up to sprint at cruise.

train/talk.note: Seated, the near hand raised into the dome glass and the head tilting, which is `talk` for somebody who cannot stand up. The hand has to clear the dome's sill to be seen at all, so the upper arm comes forward about 60 degrees and the forearm points up.

train/interact.note: Seated, the near arm reaching forward and up out of the lap toward the glass: `interact` points at what was tapped, and a passenger points out of the window.
